main_body: Flat-roofed desert building: a sand-coloured roof terrace with a teal dome on top, over a brick front wall with an arched door and a small lattice window
top_band: Sand-coloured roof surface, rows 3-33 (light #f2d3a0/#e3b77e, with a brighter lip at rows 30-33), clearly lighter than the brick face and separated from it by a dark edge at rows 34-36
evidence: Column x=32 reads as an outline at row 2, then a long sand top band (rows 3-33). Rows 30-33 form a lighter front-edge lip and rows 34-36 are a dark brown eave shadow. Below that is the brick face (rows 37-64) with its own mortar lines. The dome shows a lit hemisphere on a grey drum, so it stands on the roof and its top reads from above. The door has a pale frame and a dark inner edge, and the window has a sill and a dark lattice, so both read as inset. The roof is tall compared with a typical foreshortened top, but it reads as a flat terrace with a parapet seen from above, so I treat it as a valid 3/4 piece.

style.evidence: The outlines are tinted dark brown (0% neutral), and the sand speckle and brick variation give some texture. Flat-fill coverage is only 2%. The piece is still thinner than the references: 30 distinct colours against 66 and 185, and a median of 8 colours per tile against 11 and 18. Each material (sand, brick, teal dome) has only about 3-4 steps, against 5-6 in Beodeul. The large sand roof is mostly one tone with sparse specks, and the brick courses are fairly flat blocks. It would look slightly thinner and flatter next to the references, so I fail it.
